verdicts.opus: D and B both measured the same corpus correctly. D went further: it decomposed volume into critical share and caught the sports contamination of the 'layoffs' match. It also caught the acronym collision and the May 2026 enrichment collapse, and it shipped valid charts and a full regenerate recipe. B was accurate and well caveated, but its chart is malformed and it is thinner on drill-down. A and C had no data. A offered off-question layoff totals from memory, honestly labelled; C declined entirely.
verdicts.gpt: C best equips a decision-maker: it quantifies the volume and tone trends, shows the critical-share pattern, and surfaces the sports-heavy noise and place-coverage limits. B is careful and reproducible, but its chart and trend ceilings sharply limit the evidence presentation; C’s main weaknesses are its overlong verdict and a one-day gap calculation error.
